combos.effects: Toxic chloramine gas causes respiratory damage, chest pain, shortness of breath. High concentrations are fatal.
combos.common_scenario: Mixing bleach-based cleaners with ammonia-based glass cleaners or urine.
combos.advice: Never mix cleaning products. Use one product at a time. Ventilate well.

combos.effects: Chlorine gas was used as a chemical weapon in WWI. Causes severe lung damage, pulmonary edema, death.
combos.common_scenario: Mixing bleach with 'natural' vinegar cleaners to 'boost' cleaning power.
combos.advice: Never mix bleach with any acid, including vinegar, lemon juice, or toilet bowl cleaners.

combos.effects: Peracetic acid is corrosive to skin, eyes, and lungs. Not immediately life-threatening in household concentrations but harmful.
combos.common_scenario: Using H₂O₂ and vinegar as natural cleaners at the same time.
combos.advice: Use them separately. Apply one, rinse, then the other.

combos.effects: Chloroform causes dizziness, unconsciousness, liver damage. Chloroacetone is a lachrymatory agent (tear gas component).
combos.common_scenario: Disinfecting surfaces with bleach then wiping with alcohol, or mixing sanitizers.
combos.advice: Never combine bleach with alcohol-based products.

combos.effects: Violently exothermic. Can cause steam explosions that spray caustic liquid. Burns to skin and eyes.
combos.common_scenario: Using two different drain cleaners sequentially without rinsing.
combos.advice: Use only one drain cleaner. Flush thoroughly with water before using any other product.

combos.effects: Strong oxidizer + organic fuel = fire or explosion. The mixture can self-ignite.
combos.common_scenario: Improper storage of pool chemicals near automotive fluids.
combos.advice: Store pool chemicals in a cool, dry place away from all organic materials.

combos.effects: Adding water to concentrated H₂SO₄ causes violent boiling that splashes acid. Always add acid to water, never water to acid.
combos.advice: ALWAYS add acid to water (A to W = Acid to Water). Never the reverse.

combos.effects: Bleach degrades in heat, losing effectiveness and releasing O₂. At very high temperatures, can produce sodium chlorate which is a fire accelerant.
combos.common_scenario: Storing bleach near furnaces, in hot garages, or in direct sunlight.
combos.advice: Store bleach at room temperature, away from heat and light.
